item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is the safer merge candidate because it delivers the replayable multipart convenience API with focused changes. Both patches violate the explicit requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add, but B additionally changes global request-body and retry behavior contrary to the frozen scope.","reasons":["A reuses multipartbody.NewFile, validates inputs before requesting, preserves Add's implementation, and verifies multipart field, filename, content, and full content on both retry attempts.","B modifies RawClient.Do to eagerly buffer every non-native reader unless WithNoRetry is set, changing Add, Update, and all other raw-reader requests despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated retry refactoring and requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged.","B's global buffering can introduce unexpected memory use and moves source-reader failures from transport time to request construction across the SDK; its README and changelog advertise this out-of-scope semantic change.","B has stronger validation coverage for source-reader errors and FilesOption propagation, but those advantages do not outweigh its contract-breaking global behavior."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.","A lacks the required explicit test for source-reader failures.","The expanded Add documentation makes detailed retry claims that may couple the API documentation to transport implementation details."],"risks_b":["Upload also duplicates Add rather than delegating to it.","The RawClient change violates scope discipline and changes established streaming and error-timing semantics throughout the SDK.","The Upload retry test only drains each multipart body and does not verify the encoded content on every attempt, though separate raw retry tests cover generic replayability."]}
